import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 899

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/899](https://www.erdosproblems.com/899)
-/

open Filter Set

open scoped Pointwise Topology

namespace Erdos899

open Erdos899

/--
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A - A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} = \infty?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa [Ru78].

[Ru78] Ruzsa, I. Z., _On the cardinality of {$A+A$}\ and {$A-A$}_. (1978), 933--938.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos899.lean#L793"]
theorem erdos_899 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite →
    Tendsto (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 0) →
    atTop.limsup (fun N => ((A - A : Set ℕ) ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : EReal) /
      (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos899

reformulations.difference: The Lean expression `A - A : Set ℕ` uses truncated natural-number subtraction rather than the usual integer difference set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every positive natural d, d belongs to the natural-number difference set exactly when its integer cast belongs to the integer difference set of the cast image of A. Truncated negative differences become zero and are excluded by `Icc 1 N`. The injective integer cast therefore identifies the two counted windows, giving identical cardinalities for every N. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, `difference_window_counts` proves this equality, and `exact_source_equivalence` proves the complete statement equivalent to the formulation with integer differences, little-o, and arbitrarily large real thresholds attained arbitrarily far out. Neither proof uses the theorem under review.

review.notes:
Checked the sole declaration and found it faithful. Both uses of ncard count finite interval intersections, so the infinite-set fallback is unreachable. The density hypothesis is exactly little-o of N. For infinite A the denominator is eventually positive, making the initial zero-denominator cases harmless. The hypotheses are nonvacuous, for example for the powers of two. Lean checks verified the extended-real quotient and limsup semantics and tested small finite windows, including N = 0.

The live source was Cloudflare-blocked; its July 2026 archived page states the exact question and attributes the affirmative solution to Ruzsa. The current community database corroborates the solved/Lean status. The cited external proof compiled successfully against the installed Mathlib, with axioms exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. All scratch checks also compiled without errors, warnings, or sorry dependencies. The reviewed file was not modified.
